title: Maximal ind-etale subalgebra commutes with arbitrary field extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $A$ be any commutative unital $k$-algebra, allowing the zero algebra, and let $L/k$ be any field extension [def-pc-field-extension]. Define $B_k(A)\subseteq A$ to be the union of all unital $k$-subalgebras $D\subseteq A$ for which $\operatorname{Spec}D\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite etale [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism]; the union is a subalgebra by [lem-sfb-finite-etale-subalgebra-directed-union]. Define $B_L(A\otimes_kL)$ in the same way with base field $L$. The map induced by the inclusion $B_k(A)\subseteq A$ identifies $B_k(A)\otimes_kL$ with $B_L(A\otimes_kL)$ as an $L$-subalgebra of $A\otimes_kL$. No finite-generation, reducedness or dimension hypothesis on $A$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0CKU, label lemma-change-fields-max-weakly-etale-subalgebra; identify the maximal weakly etale subalgebra with the directed union of its finite etale subalgebras by Tag 0CKR.

proof.text: If $A=0$, both subalgebras and both tensor products in the conclusion are zero. Henceforth the arguments involving fields or nonempty spectra are applied only to nonzero rings.

For every field extension $T/k$ construct the comparison $c_{A,T}:B_k(A)\otimes_kT\to B_T(A\otimes_kT)$ inside $A\otimes_kT$. The tensor of $B_k(A)\hookrightarrow A$ is injective by the cited flatness and exactness statements. The union lemma presents $B_k(A)$ as a directed union of finite etale algebras, hence it is ind-etale by the cited definition. The stability lemma makes its base change to $T$ ind-etale and weakly etale. Every element of that base change lies in its singly generated $T$-subalgebra, which is finite etale by the weakly-etale-over-a-field lemma. Its image therefore lies in $B_T(A\otimes_kT)$. Thus $c_{A,T}$ exists and is injective. All comparisons below are this inclusion map, so their composites agree on $b\otimes t$ and respect towers of fields.

source.place: Tag 0CKU, label lemma-change-fields-max-weakly-etale-subalgebra; opening paragraph: construction of the injective comparison

proof.text: First take $A=F$ a finitely generated field extension of $k$, and $T=\Omega$ algebraically closed. By the core ring-operations lemma, $B_k(F)$ is a separable algebraic subfield of $F$. Conversely, if $\alpha\in F$ is separably algebraic over $k$, its monic minimal-polynomial relation makes $k[\alpha]$ finite-dimensional; it is a field, since the minimal polynomial is irreducible and its quotient is $k[\alpha]$. Every element of $k[\alpha]$ is separably algebraic because it lies in the relative separable closure, which is a separable subfield by the cited definition. It is therefore finite separable, hence finite etale by the finite-etale-algebra criterion, and so $\alpha\in B_k(F)$. Thus $E=B_k(F)$ is exactly the relative separable algebraic closure of $k$ in $F$. The cited finite-separable-closure lemma gives $[E:k]<\infty$ and geometric irreducibility of $F/E$.

source.place: Tag 0CKU, label lemma-change-fields-max-weakly-etale-subalgebra; final field case: identify the finite separable constant field

proof.text:
Apply the separable tensor splitting to $E/k$: choose an $\Omega$-algebra isomorphism $\theta:E\otimes_k\Omega\simeq\prod_{s\in S}\Omega$, where $S$ is finite. Each coordinate of $e\mapsto\theta(e\otimes1)$ is a $k$-embedding $\tau_s:E\to\Omega$. Tensor associativity and the finite coordinate idempotents give
$$F\otimes_k\Omega\simeq F\otimes_E(E\otimes_k\Omega)\simeq\prod_{s\in S}R_s,\qquad R_s=F\otimes_{E,\tau_s}\Omega.$$
For clarity, the second isomorphism sends $f\otimes(z_s)_s$ to $(f\otimes z_s)_s$; its inverse is the sum of the factor maps into the tensor product multiplied by the coordinate idempotents. These formulas are inverse on elementary tensors. Under this isomorphism the included $E\otimes_k\Omega$ is exactly the product of the scalar copies of $\Omega$.

source.place: Tag 0CKU, label lemma-change-fields-max-weakly-etale-subalgebra; final field case: displayed decomposition over embeddings

proof.text:
For each $s$, geometric irreducibility of $F/E$ says that $\operatorname{Spec}R_s$ is nonempty and irreducible, hence connected (a separation would give disjoint nonempty opens in an irreducible space). The connectedness-idempotent criterion and the global-sections description of an affine spectrum imply that $R_s\ne0$ has no idempotents except $0,1$. The core ring-operations lemma therefore makes $B_\Omega(R_s)$ a separable algebraic field extension of $\Omega$. Such a field equals $\Omega$: the minimal polynomial of any element is irreducible over the algebraically closed field $\Omega$, so has degree one. The finite-product clause of the same core lemma now gives
$$B_\Omega(F\otimes_k\Omega)=\prod_s B_\Omega(R_s)=\prod_s\Omega=E\otimes_k\Omega$$
as subalgebras under the preceding decomposition. This proves surjectivity of $c_{F,\Omega}$, rather than merely an abstract isomorphism of its source and target.

source.place: Tag 0CKU, label lemma-change-fields-max-weakly-etale-subalgebra; final field case: each geometric factor has scalar core; assemble finite products

proof.text:
Next let $A$ be reduced and of finite type over $k$. The zero case is settled. A field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and $k$; the finite-type-Noetherian lemma therefore makes $A$ Noetherian. The total-fractions lemma identifies $Q(A)$ with the finite product of its minimal-prime residue fields $F_i$. Each $F_i=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p_i)$ is finitely generated as a field over $k$: the images of finitely many algebra generators generate that fraction field. The localization map $A\to Q(A)$ is injective, since a fraction $a/1=0$ entails $sa=0$ for a nonzerodivisor $s$. The preceding field case, the finite-product clause for $B$, and the coordinate formulas for finite tensor products give $B_\Omega(Q(A)\otimes_k\Omega)=B_k(Q(A))\otimes_k\Omega$. By the intersection clause,
$$B_\Omega(A\otimes_k\Omega)=(A\otimes_k\Omega)\cap B_\Omega(Q(A)\otimes_k\Omega).$$
Tensoring the exact sequence $0\to A\cap B_k(Q(A))\to A\oplus B_k(Q(A))\xrightarrow{(a,b)\mapsto a-b}Q(A)$ with $\Omega$ identifies this intersection with $(A\cap B_k(Q(A)))\otimes_k\Omega=B_k(A)\otimes_k\Omega$. Flatness also supplies the ambient tensor injections. This proves the reduced finite-type case.

source.place: Tag 0CKU, label lemma-change-fields-max-weakly-etale-subalgebra; reduced finite-type case: total fractions, intersections, and exact scalar extension

proof.text: Let $A$ now be any finite-type $k$-algebra, let $N$ be its nilradical and $R=A/N$. The core lemma gives $B_k(A)\simeq B_k(R)$. The map $q:A\otimes_k\Omega\to R\otimes_k\Omega$ has kernel $N\otimes_k\Omega$ by tensor exactness. Every element of this kernel is a finite sum $\sum_j n_j\otimes\lambda_j$ with $n_j$ nilpotent; if $n_j^{m_j}=0$, its power of exponent $1+\sum_j(m_j-1)$ vanishes, by expanding the product. Thus the kernel is a nil ideal, without assuming $A\otimes_k\Omega$ reduced. Given $x\in B_\Omega(A\otimes_k\Omega)$, functoriality sends $q(x)$ into $B_\Omega(R\otimes_k\Omega)$. The reduced finite-type case and $B_k(A)\simeq B_k(R)$ provide $y\in B_k(A)\otimes_k\Omega$ with $q(y)=q(x)$. Step 2 puts $y$ in $B_\Omega(A\otimes_k\Omega)$. Hence $x-y$ is nilpotent in that reduced core, so is zero. This proves the finite-type case.

source.place: Tag 0CKU, label lemma-change-fields-max-weakly-etale-subalgebra; reduction from finite type to reduced finite type; kernel handled as a nil ideal

proof.text: For arbitrary $A$ and algebraically closed $\Omega/k$, take $x\in B_\Omega(A\otimes_k\Omega)$ and a finite etale $\Omega$-subalgebra $D$ containing it, using the union lemma. Choose a finite $\Omega$-basis $d_1,\ldots,d_r$ of $D$ and write each $d_j$ as a finite sum of elementary tensors. The finitely many coefficients from $A$ appearing in these expressions generate a finite-type $k$-subalgebra $A_0\subseteq A$. Flatness embeds $A_0\otimes_k\Omega$ in $A\otimes_k\Omega$, and every $d_j$, hence all of $D$, belongs to this subalgebra. Thus $x\in B_\Omega(A_0\otimes_k\Omega)$. The finite-type case puts $x$ in $B_k(A_0)\otimes_k\Omega\subseteq B_k(A)\otimes_k\Omega$; the last inclusion follows since every finite etale subalgebra of $A_0$ is one of $A$. No finite presentation descent or smallness assumption on a category is used: the indices are subsets of the set of subalgebras of $A$.

source.place: Tag 0CKU, label lemma-change-fields-max-weakly-etale-subalgebra; finite-type reduction, written elementwise using finite bases

proof.text:
Finally let $L/k$ be arbitrary. Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega/L$ by the cited existence lemma. By Step 2 there is a chain of inclusions inside $A\otimes_k\Omega$,
$$B_k(A)\otimes_k\Omega\longrightarrow B_L(A\otimes_kL)\otimes_L\Omega\longrightarrow B_\Omega(A\otimes_k\Omega).$$
The composite is the comparison for $\Omega/k$ and is surjective by Step 8; hence the first arrow is surjective too. It is the tensor with $\Omega$ of $c_{A,L}$. Exactness gives $(\operatorname{coker}c_{A,L})\otimes_L\Omega=0$. Tensoring an $L$-vector space $V$ with $\Omega$ detects zero: extend $1\in\Omega$ to an $L$-basis and let $p:\Omega\to L$ take its $1$-coordinate; then $(1\otimes p)(v\otimes1)=v$. Consequently $\operatorname{coker}c_{A,L}=0$. Together with its injectivity from Step 2 this proves that the specified inclusion identifies the two $L$-subalgebras for every $L/k$.

source.place: Tag 0CKU, label lemma-change-fields-max-weakly-etale-subalgebra; reduction to an algebraically closed overfield and descent of surjectivity
